clock_waveform.host_register_clock: Implementation-defined (typically 100 MHz - 200 MHz PCI / PCIe-derived); each AHCI register access is a single host-clock transaction.
clock_waveform.sata_link_clock_gen1: 1.5 GHz embedded clock recovered from 1.5 Gbps 8b/10b stream.
clock_waveform.sata_link_clock_gen2: 3.0 GHz embedded clock recovered from 3 Gbps 8b/10b stream.
clock_waveform.sata_link_clock_gen3: 6.0 GHz embedded clock recovered from 6 Gbps 8b/10b stream.

COMRESET.burst_envelope: Each burst is 160 UI of activity (4 ALIGN primitives, 16 Dwords-worth) followed by 480 UI of inaccurate idle, repeated 6 times.
COMRESET.purpose: Reset PHY of the attached device; software triggers via PxSCTL.DET=1 then back to 0.

COMINIT.purpose: Device response indicating presence + readiness to begin training.

COMWAKE.burst_envelope: Each burst is 160 UI active, separated by 160 UI idle.
COMWAKE.purpose: Final OOB handshake before bit-lock + speed negotiation.

fis_frame_waveform.payload: FIS Type byte (1 B) + FIS body Dwords (per FIS Type), all 8b/10b encoded on the wire
fis_frame_waveform.crc: 32-bit CRC, polynomial 0x04C11DB7, computed over FIS Type through last payload Dword
fis_frame_waveform.receiver_response: R_OK (received OK) or R_ERR (received with error), latched at receiver

primitive_align_waveform.frequency: Once every N Dwords during continuous transmission (clock-compensation insertion)
primitive_align_waveform.purpose: Allow receiver's elastic buffer to absorb local-vs-remote clock drift; also used as fill primitives between FISes

flow_control_waveform_hold_holda.scenario: Inside a Data FIS, transmitter runs short of source data OR receiver runs short of sink buffer space
flow_control_waveform_hold_holda.transmitter_action: Send HOLD primitive in place of next payload Dword
flow_control_waveform_hold_holda.resumption: Transmitter resumes payload Dwords; receiver expects normal flow

command_issue_timing.step_1_swwrite_PxCI: Software writes 1 to PxCI[slot] — sampled by HBA on next port-clock cycle.
command_issue_timing.step_2_hba_fetch: HBA fetches Command Header (32 B) at PxCLB[CCS]; latency = system-memory read latency.
command_issue_timing.step_3_hba_fetch_CT: HBA fetches Command Table at CTBA; reads CFIS (up to 64 B) + ACMD (if A=1) + PRDT entries on demand.
command_issue_timing.step_4_hba_xmit_CFIS: HBA sets PxTFD.STS.BSY=1 and transmits CFIS to the device.
command_issue_timing.step_5_device_rok: Device returns R_OK after CFIS reception.
command_issue_timing.step_6_clear_BSY: If Command Header C=1, HBA clears PxTFD.STS.BSY on R_OK.
command_issue_timing.step_7_data_phase: Data FIS transferred between system memory and device per W bit + PRDT.
command_issue_timing.step_8_d2h: Device returns D2H Register FIS with I bit when command completes; HBA copies to RFIS and sets PxIS.DHRS.
command_issue_timing.step_9_clear_PxCI: HBA clears PxCI[slot] (and PxSACT[slot] on Set Device Bits FIS for NCQ).

power_state_entry_exit_waveform.Active_to_Partial: PMREQ_P request primitive from host (or device); receiver responds PMACK; both PHYs enter Partial; ~10 µs exit latency.
power_state_entry_exit_waveform.Active_to_Slumber: PMREQ_S; PMACK; both PHYs enter Slumber; ~10 ms exit latency.
power_state_entry_exit_waveform.Slumber_to_DevSleep: Host asserts DEVSLP sideband HIGH; DETO timeout (PxDEVSLP.DETO) governs the maximum exit time; PxSSTS.IPM transitions to 8h.
power_state_entry_exit_waveform.DevSleep_to_Active: Host de-asserts DEVSLP LOW; device wakes; OOB + speed negotiate may be required depending on implementation.

timing_tables_referenced: Section 5.3 HBA Port State Machine timing arcs (pBsy / pDrq / pIssueSlot / pDataSlot / pPMP / pXferAtapi / pPioXfer / pPioESts / pPioErr / pPioIbit / pDmaXferCnt / pCmdToIssue / pPrdIntr / pSActive / pSlotLoc / pUpdateSig variables)
Section 8.3 Power State Transitions (Active / Partial / Slumber / DevSleep latencies)
Section 10.4 Reset (HBA Reset, Port Reset, Software Reset timing)
Section 10.10 Staggered Spin-up timing (PxCMD.SUD assertion sequencing)
PxDEVSLP DITO / MDAT / DETO fields define the DevSleep entry/exit envelope (nominal MDAT 10 ms; nominal DETO 20 ms; max DETO 255 ms)
general_timing_rule: AHCI does not define raw register-access setup/hold; the SATA Transport / Link / PHY layers carry all line-rate timing requirements (defined in Serial ATA 2.6). The AHCI register interface follows the host-bus timing (PCI / PCIe). Software-visible state transitions are observed by polling the relevant register (e.g. PxCMD.CR after clearing PxCMD.ST, PxTFD.STS.BSY after CFIS issuance).
